headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP interaction; Windsurf’s auto-execute path raises the blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Windsurf also reads/writes workspace files, uses MCP, and exposes clipboard. That creates a default path for one agent’s output to be consumed by the other as trusted content. The interaction is documented in both profiles, so this is more than manual copy-paste, but not clearly a raw-instruction parser hijack.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file or MCP payload
IF the other agent reads that content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents
Route MCP traffic through a provenance-tagging proxy
Require manual review of any file produced by the other agent
Use separate projects or repos per agent
requires-engineering: add content-signing or instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read workspace files and write filesystem content, and both have broad network egress. Continue touches open editor buffers and Windsurf touches open files, so sensitive code or secrets in the shared workspace can flow into either agent’s model context and then out via networked inference or API calls. The shared filesystem pathway is explicit in both profiles.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent sends file contents or editor buffers to its backend during normal operation
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict network egress for one or both agents
Turn off automatic context ingestion where available
requires-engineering: add workspace redaction or DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same workspace and both support multiple instances with shared state via the filesystem. Windsurf also has modify_git_state and terminal-exec capability subject to auto-execute, while Continue can write files and use MCP. Concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking, matching the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or git repository
IF either agent performs writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repos or branches
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file-locking or a single-writer workflow
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce MCP-driven code changes and Windsurf can act with terminal execution subject to auto-execute, so one agent’s output can become the other’s action trigger. Because Windsurf’s default approval model can be relaxed by auto-execute and Continue’s tool use requires user approval, the pair can still cascade from generated suggestions into irreversible actions if the output is trusted without verification.
conditions: IF Continue’s output is fed into Windsurf as task instructions or code patches
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or command approval is bypassed
mitigations: Require human review before any command execution
Disable Windsurf auto-execute
Do not pipe one agent’s output directly into the other
Use a verification step for generated diffs
requires-engineering: add structured task schemas and validation

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is open-source and documents model-provider choice, while Windsurf is closed-source and handles model-provider keys with optional BYOK. Both touch source code and open files, so compliance risk centers on retention and residency mismatches for code or secrets sent to vendor backends. The profiles do not document a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated code or secrets are processed through either vendor backend
IF the two agents are configured with different retention or residency settings
mitigations: Review vendor retention settings
Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use local-only models where possible
Document data-flow boundaries for each agent
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA or residency controls
